gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-hk: Noto Sans HK sets large lowercase forms with tight clearance above them, and the brush ends lift away before each curve closes. Nulshock above it is stretched and technical, drawn with a steady outline, so a long page of the sans would feel brisk and clear.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-imperia: Approachable and technical at once, with Nulshock stretched wide up top. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic follows with c ends that point apart like pincers, and a long page of that plain sans would feel friendly, steady and easy to move through.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-inscrip: Wide, bold and built like bent tubing, Nulshock keeps every stroke at the same gauge. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian answers with big open eyes on its e and a, so a long run of the sans would feel clean and unhurried.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-jp: Nulshock draws plain constant-width lines, stretched out with generous tracking so the whole heading feels technical and bold. Noto Sans JP, a very tall plain sans, sweeps its curves open and keeps paragraphs crisp.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Nulshock stretches out its capitals with spacious tracking, each stroke like thread stitched along a path. But Noto Sans Kaithi fills the line with lowercase forms that stand almost like capitals, so extended text reads dense, contemporary and quietly steady.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Nulshock runs wide and technical, with monoline strokes and capitals barely above the lowercase. And Noto Sans Kannada has a gentle bump up to its capitals and s curves that open at both ends, so a long passage feels approachable.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-kayah-l: Brush ends lift away before the curve closes, and capitals sit only slightly above the lowercase, which keeps everything quiet. Noto Sans Kayah Li lets a long passage move cleanly, while Nulshock above it looks as if drawn with a marker tip.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-kharosh: Nulshock is stretched wide and bold, with every stroke at the same gauge and tracking left spacious. Noto Sans Kharoshthi lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through each line, so a long passage of this plain sans feels approachable and solid.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Every stroke of Nulshock is drawn at one thickness, stretched wide with spacious tracking and a technical bite. But Noto Sans Khmer gives the plain sans side proud, almost capital-sized small letters and generous openings like chisel notches, so the heading never crowds it.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Nulshock looks like glass-tube lettering, hollow and constant in thickness, stretched wide with room between letters. Noto Sans Khojki, a plain sans with a large clear eye on every e, lets light through its wide exits and keeps the heading from overwhelming the page.
